with_residual.note: Residual inflated on binary scale (absorbs Bernoulli within-cell noise)

interpretation.key_finding: Top-3 SET {item_id, model:item_id, residual} is recovered in 100% of simulations. However, exact ORDERING differs: residual is always #1 on binary scale due to Bernoulli noise absorption, whereas observed data shows item_id > model:item_id > residual.
interpretation.residual_inflation: Binary probit simulation inflates residual from observed 25.0% to simulated 47.5%, while compressing item_id (37.9% -> 23.9%) and model:item_id (30.2% -> 23.9%). This is the known Bernoulli ceiling effect.
interpretation.systematic_ranking: Excluding residual, item_id and model:item_id are ALWAYS the top 2 systematic sources (100%), competing at ~50/50 for #1 vs #2 position. The observed item_id > model:item_id ordering is recovered 48% of the time.
interpretation.implication: The binary simulation confirms that Henderson I reliably identifies the CORRECT SET of dominant variance sources even on binary data, but the within-set ordering is distorted by Bernoulli residual inflation. The real data's ranking (item_id > model:item_id > residual) reflects genuine item difficulty structure that is strong enough to overcome the Bernoulli floor.
